key_concept: Chromosomes become fully condensed by diakinesis, the last sub-stage of prophase I, and it is meiosis II (not meiosis I) that resembles mitosis.
steps: Prophase I has five sub-stages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Chromosomes condense progressively through these stages.
In diakinesis, the final sub-stage of prophase I, chromosomes are fully condensed, chiasmata terminalise and the meiotic spindle assembles. So Statement I is correct.
Meiosis I is a reductional division ($2n \rightarrow n$). Homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis), cross over and then separate, which does not happen in mitosis.
Meiosis II is an equational division in which sister chromatids separate, exactly as in mitosis. So meiosis II, not meiosis I, resembles mitosis. Statement II is false.
Statement I is true and Statement II is false, so the answer is Option (3).
final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
why_not_others: Options (1) and (4) treat Statement II as true, which confuses meiosis I with meiosis II. Option (2) wrongly rejects the fact that condensation is complete by diakinesis.
common_trap: Students swap meiosis I and meiosis II and mark 'meiosis I resembles mitosis' as true.
time_saving_tip: Remember the pairing: meiosis I is reductional and unlike mitosis, while meiosis II is equational and mitosis-like. This alone eliminates options (1) and (4).
